items.title: No comparison of the clinic with usual advice in first-opinion practice
items.whyItMatters: Clinic data describe completers only and the one trial was in referral practice.
items.opportunity: Compare the clinic with usual advice across the group's practices in a pragmatic trial.

items.title: Owner-reported outcomes are open to expectation bias
items.whyItMatters: Owners report improvement from expectation alone (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Add lameness scored from video by a vet unaware of allocation, and body weight.

items.title: Dogs drop out of weight clinics
items.whyItMatters: Most dogs stop attending before six months (claim c4), which would bias a completers-only comparison.
items.opportunity: Collect the six-month outcome by phone and at a single review visit for every dog, whatever its attendance.

items.title: Cost of diet and visits falls unevenly on owners
items.whyItMatters: Owners on low incomes or far from a practice may not keep attending.
items.opportunity: Provide the discounted diet to both groups and record distance and payment concerns.

items.title: Welfare costs of calorie restriction
items.whyItMatters: Hunger behaviours are common and may reflect welfare costs.
items.opportunity: Record hunger behaviours as a balancing outcome.

errorsFound: The board's case for roll-out rests on clinic completers; the retrieved attendance data show most dogs stop before six months.
reevaluation: The gaps support a pragmatic trial with central allocation, an owner-reported primary outcome backed by blinded lameness and weight, intention-to-treat follow-up and welfare measures.
summary: Five gaps: no first-opinion comparison, expectation bias, attrition, owner cost and welfare.
